answer: The system requires submissions to match a specific burst pattern. Like a crystal lattice resolving under pressure, the ledger expects peaks every forty milliseconds. At the same interval, a control signal pulses from a network node called juniper. If an agent sends data in a uniform stream, the system flags it as synthetic. This constant flow mimics raven wings beating without pause. The attacker must throttle their output to mimic human jitter. Each identity requires unique random delays calculated live. This adds significant latency to every transaction.
